instrument.title: Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting

austrian_notification_layers.source: Austrian reservations and notifications at ratification

bilateral_adjudication_method: identify treaty as a potential Covered Tax Agreement from Austria's current notification layers
verify the partner jurisdiction's MLI party/signatory status and its own CTA notification
match reservations and optional provisions on both sides article by article
resolve changes caused by Austria's 2023 notification/reservation amendment
determine entry into force for both jurisdictions
determine Article 35 effective date specifically for withholding taxes
cross-check against the current Austrian synthesized treaty text where available
record only mutually effective WHT-relevant modifications as legal effects

wht_relevant_article_seed.article_7_ppt: evaluate pair-specific matching; standard cross-cutting abuse condition alone does not create elevated review classification
wht_relevant_article_seed.article_8_dividend_transfer_transactions: evaluate pair-specific matching and any reservations/holding-period interaction
wht_relevant_article_seed.other_articles: retain only where they can affect dividend, interest, royalty entitlement, beneficial ownership/treaty access, or source-country WHT treatment

release_constraints: Austria-side CTA notification is not sufficient evidence of bilateral MLI effect.
The BMF implementation counts are contextual snapshots and must not be used as a production relationship inventory.
No MLI article effect may be promoted without bilateral matching.
No withholding-tax MLI effect may be promoted without pair-specific Article 35 effective-date analysis.
A synthesized treaty text is strong pair-level implementation evidence where available but does not replace preservation of the underlying instrument chain.
